solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Asian I expect is put in the shade

indicators.note: is put in says the guessing phrase goes inside the colour word

parts.note: tan is a shade of light brown
'I bet' is a casual way of saying I expect

explanation.surface: Someone from Asia is overshadowed, or kept out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in the shade' looks like one idiom meaning outshone, but it splits: I BET goes inside TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tibetan is a native of Tibet, a region of Asia, so an example of an Asian.

clue.text: Italian chant, second half first

indicators.note: the instruction says the back half of the chant word is moved to the front

parts.note: cantus is a Latin term for a chant or melody, as in plainsong

explanation.surface: An instruction for rearranging a piece of Italian singing.
explanation.walkthrough: CANTUS split as CAN and TUS becomes TUS + CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tuscan is a person from Tuscany, a region of central Italy.

clue.text: Those proscribing flags

definitions.meaning: people who ban or forbid things

explanation.surface: Censors who forbid the waving of flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is both one who bans and a flag or standard, a play on two senses.

clue.text: Whatshisname a beanpole, struggling to chew?

parts.note: a beanpole is a very thin person, so the word describing one is thin
someone gummy has no teeth and so struggles to chew

explanation.surface: Trying to recall the name of a lanky person who can't eat properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are placeholder words used when a person's or thing's name escapes you.

clue.text: Yuetide, might you say?

indicators.note: a question about how one might say it signals that the description is spoken aloud

parts.note: the clue's Yuetide is the Christmas season word with no L, so it is the season with 'no L'

explanation.surface: A misspelt word for the Christmas season, queried.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint is deliberate: Yuletide missing its L is 'no L', and saying that gives the carol word for Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a traditional word for Christmas, the Yuletide festival, found in carols.

clue.text: Adversary is following me into hideout that's not closed

indicators.note: following says the word is comes after what precedes it
into says the pronoun goes inside the shortened hideout
not closed means the hideout word loses its last letter, left open at the end

parts.note: a nest is a hideout, as in a nest of thieves
taken as written

explanation.surface: An enemy has tracked me to a hideaway whose door is open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not closed' drops the last letter, as an open-ended hideout; 'is following' puts IS at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A nemesis is an arch-enemy or rival who cannot be beaten.

clue.text: Removal of pests in particular?

parts.note: literally the picking out of head lice eggs; figuratively being overly particular about small faults

explanation.surface: A question about one specific form of pest control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In particular' seems to mean specifically, but particular means fussy here.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantic fault-finding, literally the grooming removal of lice eggs, a hyphenated idiom.

clue.text: Children's author left at the coalface?

indicators.note: being at the coalface means being in the pit, so the side letter goes inside it

parts.note: the coalface is the working part of a mine

explanation.surface: A writer for children who has walked away from mining work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed, but it is just L placed inside MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne wrote the Winnie-the-Pooh stories for young readers.

clue.text: Withdraw score

definitions.meaning: pull out of a race or contest
to scrape or mark a surface

explanation.surface: Pull out and record the points, or cancel the goal.
explanation.definitionFit: To scratch is both to withdraw from a contest and to mark a line, as scoring does.

clue.text: Soak was a poser on uppers initially (and speed!)

parts.note: an artist's model sits, so one who posed sat

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the drug word

parts.note: rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A model gets drenched while high on stimulants and amphetamines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uppers' and 'speed' look like a drug theme, but speed is simply RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To saturate something is to soak it completely, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Frightful tale set in outskirts of Manhattan is mawkish

indicators.note: frightful suggests a mess, so the letters are thrown into a new order
outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters of the city name

explanation.surface: A scary story set on the edges of New York is soppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set in' looks like a container signal, but SET and IN are anagram fodder alongside TALE and M, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish and sentimental both mean sickly, excessively emotional.

clue.text: Garbage decay

explanation.surface: Rubbish that is rotting away.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot means nonsense as well as the process of decomposing.

clue.text: Gave pen out, but missing penny to repay

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered, put out of place
missing means the penny letter is taken away

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: Someone handed over a pen but was short of the cash to pay back.
explanation.walkthrough: PEN without P leaves EN; with GAVE these letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to repay it by inflicting punishment in return.

clue.text: Luxury, light tree houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the conifer word holds the match word

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree
a vesta is a kind of match, used to light things

explanation.surface: Upmarket treehouses with lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: A vesta is an old-fashioned match, a crossword staple for 'light'; 'houses' means the tree word contains it.
explanation.definitionFit: Five-star accommodation is the top grade of hotel, used attributively for luxury.

clue.text: Exhausted — as may be the departing stage performers?

definitions.text: as may be the departing stage performers?
definitions.meaning: actors leaving the stage may be applauded as they go

explanation.surface: Tired actors receiving applause as they exit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapped-out is British slang for worn out, and literally applauded on the way off.

clue.text: Film title is OK, Home Base

indicators.note: base means debased or corrupt, so the preceding words are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: Approving the name of a movie, with a sports cry about home base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title' seems to belong with Film, but it is fodder along with IS, OK and HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Wilder's 1959 comedy with Marilyn Monroe, Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon.

clue.text: Repeating it, Queen musical sent up

parts.note: taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the musical's name is written bottom to top

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice musical

explanation.surface: A queen keeps doing it while a musical is mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' looks like mocked, but reverses EVITA to ATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterative describes a process that repeats steps over and over.

clue.text: Moving image has come into play

definitions.note: an image that conveys feeling, moving in the emotional sense

indicators.note: putting letters into play lets them move freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A film has started being shown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving image' suggests film, but moving here means expressing emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley-face symbol is a little picture expressing emotion.

clue.text: Lucrative things one invested in well, the tops!

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the number word goes into the exclamation

parts.note: my! and well! are both exclamations of surprise
taken as written
tops are spinning toys, so spinners

explanation.surface: Profitable assets, with a well and best of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' is not a water source but an exclamation, like 'my!'; 'invested in' is a container signal, not finance.
explanation.definitionFit: A money-spinner is something that brings in plenty of income.

clue.text: Ignore name in waiting to install leader of government

indicators.note: to install means to put the initial letter inside the waiting word

parts.note: elect after a title means chosen but not yet in office, waiting to take up the post

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter

explanation.surface: Passing over a nominee who is about to head the government.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes inside ELECT to make EGLECT, after N.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to ignore or fail to attend to it.

clue.text: Composer, one adding colour?

definitions.meaning: Sir John ..., English Victorian composer of The Crucifixion
someone who applies dye or tint to wood or fabric

explanation.surface: A musician who livens things up.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stainer was a composer; also, literally, anyone who stains things.

clue.text: Chicken and mustard

definitions.meaning: the bright colour of the condiment

explanation.surface: A dish of poultry with a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly and is also the colour of mustard.

clue.text: Fancy stealing funny things

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are dressed up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Wanting to shoplift some amusing items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb meaning desire, but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tag lines are punchlines or witty catchphrases, comic remarks.

clue.text: Force politician to get garlanded up?

indicators.note: to get here means to receive within, so the Member goes inside the flower ring
in a down clue, up means the garland word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Compelling an MP to wear flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reverses the garland in this down clue, giving IEL; 'to get' has the politician received inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone to act, a synonym of compel.

clue.text: Residence housing foremost of aristocrats?

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the dwelling word contains the letter

parts.note: a place is a residence, as in come back to my place

indicators.note: foremost of picks the opening letter

explanation.surface: A home occupied by leading nobles.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside PLACE; and the whole clue describes a palace too.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is the grand official home of royalty or the nobility.

clue.text: It's maximal, I fear, for a stretch?

definitions.text: It's maximal, I fear, for a stretch?

indicators.note: it's stands for it has, so the following words contain the letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grim forecast of the longest possible prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'It's' as the definition, which cannot mean a term; 'It's' (it has) is the hidden signal and the whole clue describes the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A life sentence is the heaviest prison term, slang 'stretch' meaning a jail term.

clue.text: Line that's said — as a hint

indicators.note: that's said tells us the line word is spoken aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: a queue is a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: An actor's prompt delivered as a suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' looks theatrical, but it is QUEUE, sounding like the prompt word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a signal or prompt, so a hint to act.

clue.text: Expert seeing a line pencilled in

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
vision is the faculty of seeing

explanation.surface: A specialist examining a sketch line drawn in pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pencilled in is tentative or provisional, easily rubbed out later.

clue.text: Hospital having withdrawn from charity programme sent back letter

indicators.note: sent back means the remaining letters are written in reverse order
having withdrawn from says the hospital letter leaves the programme word

parts.note: a telethon is a long TV fundraising broadcast
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital pulls out of a fundraising show and returns a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: TELETHON without H is TELETON, which reversed gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded sheet for a short written note.

clue.text: English relative found in wood, one raised in surprising circumstances?

definitions.note: something lifted when someone is surprised

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the tree word

parts.note: yew is a wood, a tree used for longbows
bro is short for brother

explanation.surface: An English relative discovered in a forest, brought up in odd circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' suggests upbringing, but means lifted: we raise this when surprised.
explanation.definitionFit: People lift the hairy arch above the eye in surprise.
